narrative:
The model estimated a 29.0% probability that you would be a bad credit risk. That is not a certainty, but under the bank’s lending threshold it was high enough for the application to be denied.

The most influential factor was the business purpose of your loan, which actually worked in your favour and lowered the estimated risk; business loans are relatively uncommon among approved applicants (8.7%). The second and most adverse factor was your checking account status: a balance of 0–200 DM pushed the prediction toward bad credit. Your time at your present residence, four years versus an approved-applicant average of about three, was the third most influential factor and also reduced the estimated risk. Overall, the favourable signals from the loan purpose and residential stability were not enough to offset the risk indicated by your checking account status, so the model still placed you above the denial threshold.

To improve a future application, focus on strengthening your checking account position and provide recent statements showing a steadier or higher balance. Ask the bank whether a smaller request, additional security, or a guarantor would help, and consider reapplying once your account history and savings look stronger.
